title: How Redheads Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss redheads: a study by sex researcher Dr. Werner Habermehl (transcribed as "hopper Mill" and "harber Mill") at the University of Hamburg claiming redheads, and people who dye their hair red, have more active sex lives, and the 2000s "redheads going extinct" claims (Oxford Hair Institute, 2005 and 2007), which they say are not true. They explain the MC1R gene mutation, its recessive inheritance, and the pigments pheomelanin (overproduced) and eumelanin (underproduced). A 2002 University of Louisville study found redheads need more anesthetic (desflurane), using electric shocks to test pain under anesthesia on 10 redheads and 10 brunettes; a later study reportedly found the same in men. They discuss possible reasons (pain hormones, pigment overstimulating pain receptors) and pharmacogenetics as a possible route to redhead-specific anesthesia. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about a top ten list from listener Greg Storkin and man crushes, and a plug for the show's mailing address.
topics: red hair and sex life study

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor tease
segments.summary: Hosts open the show, Josh admits his admiration for sex researcher Dr. Habermehl, and they introduce the topic of redheads.

segments.title: Redheads and sex lives study
segments.summary: Josh describes a study by Dr. Habermehl at the University of Hamburg, reported in the Daily Mail, claiming redheads, and women who dye their hair red, have more active sex lives. They joke about infidelity implications and Chuck's wife's past red hair.

segments.title: Redheads extinction claims
segments.summary: The hosts discuss 2005 and 2007 news reports that redheads would go extinct by 2060, attributed to the Oxford Hair Institute, and state this is not true, though an evolutionary bottleneck could make it possible.

segments.title: Genetics of red hair
segments.summary: Explanation of red hair as a phenotype caused by a recessive mutation in the MC1R gene, which leads to overproduction of pheomelanin and underproduction of eumelanin. Recessive traits can skip generations.

segments.title: Redheads and anesthesia study
segments.summary: A University of Louisville study compared 10 redheads and 10 brunettes under desflurane anesthesia, using electric shocks to test pain response, finding redheads needed more anesthetic. Another later study reportedly found the same in men, and the MC1R link to anesthesia was noted.

segments.title: Why redheads need more anesthesia
segments.summary: The hosts discuss possible explanations: the MC1R gene's link to pain-stimulating hormones, and pigments overstimulating pain receptors in the brain. They note anesthesia is not fully understood.

segments.title: Pharmacogenetics and redhead-specific anesthesia
segments.summary: The hosts mention that the study may spur development of redhead-tailored anesthesia through pharmacogenetics, and discuss the ethical controversy of genetic testing.

segments.title: Listener mail: Greg Storkin's top ten list
segments.summary: Chuck reads listener Greg Storkin's top ten reasons he is obsessed with the show, and the hosts discuss man crushes and invite listener mail.

segments.title: Sign-off and mailing address
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send mail and ask for the show's email address, then close the episode.
